elements.justification: 'Electric scooter' is defined by DEF-NRS-484B-018 as 'a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on in an upright or seated position and propelled by its electric motor or by propulsion provided by the rider', within the jurisdiction's limits of weight (not more than 100 pounds) and maximum motor speed (not more than 20 miles per hour). The word names one road-user class, and the ontology carries that class with its own local atom ru.electric_scooter, 'a standing or seated electric scooter with handlebars', whose scope is the class as the target jurisdiction's own taxonomy names it, so the definition's weight and design-speed limits are the taxonomy that atom already labels. The ru.aggregate contract says it is 'not a stand-in for a named road-user class for which the applicable definitions ... permit its own class atom — that class's own atom'. The earlier claim ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter cannot be used by any faithful rule: the run's reading leaves the aggregate with no included class, so membership is never true and the subject's class never holds in any scene. That claim is therefore replaced by the class atom the rule reads.

'roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'. 'bicycle lane, path' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'. A 'route' for these devices runs on roadways and bicycle lanes or paths, so it adds no place beyond them. rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the scooter on the region of either kind; each region quantifier ranges over the claimed kind. 'bicycle' here names the kind of structure, not road users the duty counts.
kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s), is compared with the law's own figure, 15 miles per hour, a literal. Its contract has no 'not a stand-in for' clause bearing on this quantity.

residues.why: The ordinance the words name is LVMC 11.40.185(A), posted as DEF-LVMC-11-40-185-A: 'an electric bicycle or an electric scooter may be operated on a public roadway or sidewalk, or a lane, path, or route designated for bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter use'. It provides where a scooter may be operated and states no speed. Nothing in it provides otherwise on the speed this line bounds, so the duty is the same whether or not the exception's words hold.

The permission to operate adds no restriction to the speed bound: a scooter at rest and one moving below the bound both meet it. The duty is therefore the same whether or not the scooter is being operated.

applicability: The subject is an electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter), and at the observation its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway (st.roadway) or a bicycle lane or path (st.bicycle_lane_or_path).
obligation: The subject's speed (kin.speed) is at most the literal 15 mph at the observation.

narrowings.why: The permission 'may be operated ... at a speed of not more than 15 miles per hour' is read as its limit: operating in these places above the figure is outside what the line permits.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on a roadway at 8 m/s, above 15 mph.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides in a bicycle lane at 5 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on a sidewalk at 8 m/s and overlaps no roadway, bicycle lane or path.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on a roadway, and the source does not observe its speed.
